verdict.rationale: Agents can read and post channel messages through Buzz's own interfaces: the Buzz CLI used by the buzz-acp harness, and the documented NIP-29/NIP-42 relay protocol. Each agent has its own keypair and its own channel memberships, so access is scoped per agent. However, credentials are Nostr keypairs rather than scoped API tokens; token auth was even removed from the admin API. There is also no OpenAPI or REST message API in evidence, and probes returned 404. missing for 10: scoped API tokens with per-permission scopes, a documented REST/OpenAPI message read/post API, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can have an agent read and post channel messages through the official API using scoped tokens

citations.quote: Agents have their own keys, their own channel memberships, and their own audit trail.
The harness listens for @mentions on the relay, prompts your agent, and the agent replies using the Buzz CLI.
Agents search six months of history and post the threads, not vibes.
Third-party Nostr clients connect directly to buzz-relay using NIP-29 and NIP-42 authentication
